tour.overview:
Da Nang, Vietnam's third city, sits on a bay between mountains and long beaches. In 1919 the French built a hill station at Ba Na, 1,400 metres up in the Truong Son mountains, to escape the summer heat; today its peaks are reached by cable cars and crowned with gardens, a mock French village and the Golden Bridge, opened in 2018, a gold-railed footbridge that seems to be held up by two enormous, moss-covered hands. Between the city and Hoi An rise the Marble Mountains, five limestone and marble hills named after the five elements, full of caves and Buddhist shrines.

This private day combines both with a guide and a car, and ends at the Son Tra peninsula, where a white statue of the Lady Buddha watches over the bay.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Da Nang or Hoi An
• Type: private tour with guide, car and driver, cable car
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; steps and climbs in the Marble Mountains

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Ba Na Hills cable car.
• The Golden Bridge.
• The Le Jardin d'Amour gardens and the Linh Ung pagoda of Ba Na.
• The Marble Mountains: Huyen Khong cave and Tam Thai pagoda.
• Son Tra peninsula and the Lady Buddha.

WHY THIS WORKS
We take the first cable cars of the morning to see the Golden Bridge before the crowds and the clouds, then come down for the Marble Mountains in the afternoon.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, photographers and anyone staying in Da Nang or Hoi An.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer history and culture, choose our Hue or My Son tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Ba Na Hills is a commercial resort with a theme park; we focus on the bridge, gardens and views. It is much cooler at the top: bring a jacket. Fog can cover the bridge, especially in the afternoon and the rainy season.

days.name: The Ba Na Hills cable car and Golden Bridge, lunch, the Marble Mountains and the Lady Buddha of Son Tra
days.description:
What to expect: the mountain and coast around Da Nang, with a private guide, car, cable car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:00 and drive west into the mountains, about 45 minutes from Da Nang. You board one of the first cable cars of the day for a ride of almost 6 kilometres, climbing over waterfalls and rainforest to more than 1,400 metres. At the top you walk onto the Golden Bridge, 150 metres long, curving through the air above the forest, its gold railings held by two giant hands that look carved from ancient stone. On clear mornings you see across the mountains to the sea.

You explore the French-era gardens of Le Jardin d'Amour, the wine cellar built by the French, the Linh Ung pagoda with its large seated Buddha, and the mock French village with its cathedral and squares. After lunch with a view of the mountains, you take the cable car down and drive to the Marble Mountains, between Da Nang and Hoi An.

A lift takes you up Thuy Son, the Water Mountain, the largest of the five. You visit Tam Thai pagoda, climb to viewpoints over the beach and the other peaks, and descend into Huyen Khong cave, a vast natural chamber lit by an opening in the roof, where a Buddha sits among altars and incense smoke drifts in the light. At the foot of the mountain, stone-carving workshops continue an old tradition. You end on the Son Tra peninsula, the 'monkey mountain', where the white statue of the Lady Buddha, 67 metres tall, stands at Linh Ung pagoda overlooking the bay, and where you may see rare red-shanked douc langurs in the forest. You are back at your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
07:45 – Ba Na Hills cable car.
08:30 – Golden Bridge.
09:15 – Gardens, pagoda and French village.
11:45 – Lunch.
13:00 – Cable car down.
14:00 – Marble Mountains.
15:30 – Son Tra peninsula and the Lady Buddha.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The theme park rides at Ba Na Hills are included in the ticket if you want to try them.
• Fog is common; the early cable car gives the best chance of clear views.
• An evening at the Dragon Bridge, which breathes fire on weekend nights, can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, Ba Na Hills cable car, Marble Mountains ticket and lift, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, wax museum, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the cable car included?
faq.answer: Yes, the Ba Na Hills ticket including the cable cars, gardens and theme park, plus the Marble Mountains ticket and lift.

faq.question: Will the Golden Bridge be in fog?
faq.answer: It can be, especially in the afternoon and from September to December. Taking the first cable cars gives the best chance of clear views.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at Ba Na Hills. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, very. Children love the cable car, the giant hands and the caves. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The cable car and the bridge are easy; the Marble Mountains have a lift but also many steps inside caves.

faq.question: Is Ba Na Hills touristy?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a commercial resort. We focus on the bridge, the cable car and the gardens, which are spectacular.

faq.question: What is the temperature at the top?
faq.answer: Often 15 to 20 °C, much cooler than the coast. Bring a jacket.

faq.question: Will we be taken to marble shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops; you can look at the workshops freely.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, a jacket for the mountain, comfortable shoes and covering clothes for the pagodas.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: February to August for clearer weather. From September to December rain and fog are frequent.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
